```{python}
def prepare_gamma_target(
    series: pd.Series,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Prepare a target series for Gamma-family models.

    Ensures strictly positive values by applying a small shift if needed.

    Args:
        series: Input target series.
        epsilon: Small positive constant added when zeros are present.

    Returns:
        A strictly positive pandas Series.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If series is empty or contains negative values.
    """
    if series is None or series.empty:
        raise ValueError("Input series is empty.")

    if (series < 0).any():
        raise ValueError(
            "Gamma distribution does not support negative values."
        )

    series = series.copy()

    if (series == 0).any():
        series = series + epsilon

    return series


def plot_forecast_vs_actual(
    y_train: pd.Series,
    y_test: pd.Series,
    y_pred_train: Optional[pd.Series] = None,
    y_pred_test: Optional[pd.Series] = None,
    y_pred_test_lower: Optional[pd.Series] = None,
    y_pred_test_upper: Optional[pd.Series] = None,
    model_name: str = "",
    figsize: Tuple[int, int] = (12, 6)
) -> None:
    """Plot actual and predicted values for train and test sets with confidence intervals.

    The function draws the full time series from train and test, and
    overlays the predictions if they are provided. Confidence intervals
    are shown as shaded bands for the test set. The plot is
    generated using Plotly with legend interaction enabled.

    Args:
        y_train: True target values for the training period.
        y_test: True target values for the test period.
        y_pred_train: Predicted values for the training period.
        y_pred_test: Predicted values for the test period.
        y_pred_test_lower: Lower confidence interval for test predictions.
        y_pred_test_upper: Upper confidence interval for test predictions.
        model_name: Name of the model to show in the title.
        figsize: Size of the figure in inches (width, height).

    Raises:
        TypeError: If y_train or y_test are not pandas Series.
    """
    if not isinstance(y_train, pd.Series):
        raise TypeError("Parameter 'y_train' must be a pandas Series.")
    if not isinstance(y_test, pd.Series):
        raise TypeError("Parameter 'y_test' must be a pandas Series.")

    # Convert figsize (inches) roughly to pixels for plotly
    width_px = int(figsize[0] * 80)
    height_px = int(figsize[1] * 80)

    fig = go.Figure()

    # Train actual (black solid)
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=y_train.index,
            y=y_train.values,
            mode="lines",
            name="Train (actual)",
            line=dict(color="black", width=2),
        )
    )

    # Test actual (black solid)
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=y_test.index,
            y=y_test.values,
            mode="lines",
            name="Test (actual)",
            line=dict(color="black", width=2),
        )
    )

    # Train predicted (blue dashed - GLARMA)
    if y_pred_train is not None:
        y_pred_train = y_pred_train.reindex(y_train.index)
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=y_pred_train.index,
                y=y_pred_train.values,
                mode="lines",
                name="Train (predicted)",
                line=dict(color="royalblue", dash="dash"),
            )
        )

    # Test predicted confidence interval (light blue band)
    if y_pred_test_upper is not None and y_pred_test_lower is not None:
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=y_pred_test_upper.index.tolist() + y_pred_test_lower.index.tolist()[::-1],
                y=y_pred_test_upper.values.tolist() + y_pred_test_lower.values.tolist()[::-1],
                fill="toself",
                fillcolor="rgba(65, 105, 225, 0.2)",  # Light royalblue with transparency
                line=dict(color="rgba(255,255,255,0)"),
                showlegend=True,
                name="95% CI",
            )
        )

    # Test predicted (blue dashed - GLARMA)
    if y_pred_test is not None:
        y_pred_test = y_pred_test.reindex(y_test.index)
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                x=y_pred_test.index,
                y=y_pred_test.values,
                mode="lines",
                name="Test (predicted)",
                line=dict(color="royalblue", dash="dash"),
            )
        )

    title = "Actual vs. Predicted"
    if model_name:
        title += f" - {model_name}"

    fig.update_layout(
        title=title,
        xaxis_title="Time",
        yaxis_title=target,
        width=width_px,
        height=height_px,
        legend=dict(
            orientation="v",
            yanchor="top",
            y=0.99,
            xanchor="left",
            x=0.01,
        ),
        template="plotly_white",
        hovermode="x unified",
    )

    # Adicionar destaque cinza para o período de testes
    fig.add_vrect(
        x0=y_test.index[0],
        x1=y_test.index[-1],
        fillcolor="lightgray",
        opacity=0.2,
        layer="below",
        line_width=0,
    )

    fig.show()


def rolling_prediction_glarma_like_train(
    result,
    y_train: pd.Series,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Compute in-sample rolling 1-step-ahead predictions for training data.

    Each prediction at time t is based only on information up to t-1,
    ensuring a fair comparison with rolling forecasts on the test set.
    """
    predictions = []

    for t in range(1, len(y_train)):
        pred = result.get_prediction(
            start=y_train.index[t],
            end=y_train.index[t],
            dynamic=y_train.index[t - 1],
        ).predicted_mean.iloc[0]

        predictions.append(float(np.exp(pred)))

    predictions = [np.nan] + predictions

    return pd.Series(
        predictions,
        index=y_train.index,
        name="glarma_like_train_pred",
    )


def rolling_forecast_glarma_like(
    result,
    y_train: pd.Series,
    y_test: pd.Series,
) -> Tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series, pd.Series]:
    """Rolling 1-step-ahead forecast for GLARMA-like Gamma(log) model.
    
    Returns: (predictions, lower_conf, upper_conf)
    """
    predictions = []
    lower_bounds = []
    upper_bounds = []
    current_result = result

    for t in range(len(y_test)):
        # 1-step-ahead forecast with confidence intervals (log-scale)
        forecast_obj = current_result.get_forecast(steps=1)
        pred_log = forecast_obj.predicted_mean.iloc[0]
        
        # Confidence interval (default 95%)
        conf_int = forecast_obj.conf_int().iloc[0]
        lower_log = conf_int[0]
        upper_log = conf_int[1]
        
        # Convert from log scale back to original scale
        predictions.append(float(np.exp(pred_log)))
        lower_bounds.append(float(np.exp(lower_log)))
        upper_bounds.append(float(np.exp(upper_log)))

        # Atualiza o estado com o valor observado
        observed_log = np.log(y_test.iloc[t])
        current_result = current_result.append(
            [observed_log],
            refit=False,
        )

    return (
        pd.Series(predictions, index=y_test.index, name="glarma_pred"),
        pd.Series(lower_bounds, index=y_test.index, name="glarma_lower"),
        pd.Series(upper_bounds, index=y_test.index, name="glarma_upper"),
    )


def compute_glarma_residuals(
    result,
    y: pd.Series,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Compute residuals for GLARMA-like Gamma(log) model.

    Residuals are computed in the linear predictor (log) scale:
    residual_t = log(y_t) - E[log(y_t) | F_{t-1}]
    """
    y_log = np.log(y)

    fitted_log = result.fittedvalues.reindex(y.index)

    residuals = y_log - fitted_log

    return pd.Series(
        residuals,
        index=y.index,
        name="glarma_residuals_log",
    )


def residuals_diagnostics(
    residuals: pd.Series,
    lags: int = 10,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Statistical diagnostics for GLARMA residuals."""
    res = residuals.dropna()

    # Ljung-Box test
    lb = acorr_ljungbox(res, lags=[lags], return_df=True)

    # Jarque-Bera test (SciPy >= 1.8)
    jb_stat, jb_p = jarque_bera(res)

    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Statistic": [
                lb["lb_stat"].iloc[0],
                jb_stat,
            ],
            "p-value": [
                lb["lb_pvalue"].iloc[0],
                jb_p,
            ],
        },
        index=[
            f"Ljung-Box (lag {lags})",
            "Jarque-Bera",
        ],
    )


def calculate_metrics(
    y_true: pd.Series,
    y_pred: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Calculate MAE, RMSE, and MAPE metrics.

    Args:
        y_true: Actual values.
        y_pred: Predicted values.

    Returns:
        DataFrame with metrics.
    """
    # Align indices and remove NaN values
    aligned_true = y_true.reindex(y_pred.index)
    valid_mask = ~(aligned_true.isna() | y_pred.isna())
    
    y_true_clean = aligned_true[valid_mask]
    y_pred_clean = y_pred[valid_mask]

    # MAE: Mean Absolute Error
    mae = np.mean(np.abs(y_true_clean - y_pred_clean))

    # RMSE: Root Mean Squared Error
    rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((y_true_clean - y_pred_clean) ** 2))

    # MAPE: Mean Absolute Percentage Error
    mape = np.mean(np.abs((y_true_clean - y_pred_clean) / y_true_clean)) * 100

    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Metric": ["MAE", "RMSE", "MAPE (%)"],
            "Value": [mae, rmse, mape],
        }
    )


def plot_glarma_diagnostics(
    residuals: pd.Series,
    model_name: str = "",
    figsize: Tuple[int, int] = (15, 8),
    nlags: int = 24,
) -> None:
    """Plot diagnostic panel for GLARMA-like Gamma(log) model residuals using matplotlib.

    The panel includes:
    1) Residuals over time
    2) ACF of residuals
    3) PACF of residuals
    4) Histogram of residuals
    5) Q–Q plot

    Args:
        residuals: Residuals in log-scale.
        model_name: Name of the model for the title.
        figsize: Size of the figure in inches (width, height).
        nlags: Number of lags for ACF and PACF.
    """
    res = residuals.dropna()

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=figsize)
    fig.suptitle(
        f"Diagnostics - {model_name}" if model_name else "Diagnostics",
        fontsize=14,
        y=1.00,
    )

    # 1) Residuals over time
    axes[0, 0].plot(res.index, res.values, lw=1)
    axes[0, 0].axhline(y=0, color="r", linestyle="--", lw=1)
    axes[0, 0].set_title("Residuals over time")
    axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("Residual (log scale)")
    axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
    plt.setp(axes[0, 0].xaxis.get_majorticklabels(), rotation=45, ha='right')

    # 2) ACF
    axes[0, 1].clear()
    plot_acf(res, lags=nlags, ax=axes[0, 1])
    axes[0, 1].set_title("ACF")

    # 3) PACF
    axes[0, 2].clear()
    plot_pacf(res, lags=nlags, ax=axes[0, 2], method="ywm")
    axes[0, 2].set_title("PACF")

    # 4) Histogram
    axes[1, 0].hist(res.values, bins=30, edgecolor="black", alpha=0.7)
    axes[1, 0].set_title("Histogram of residuals")
    axes[1, 0].set_xlabel("Residual")
    axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("Frequency")

    # 5) Q-Q plot
    qq = stats.probplot(res, dist="norm")
    axes[1, 1].scatter(qq[0][0], qq[0][1], alpha=0.6, s=30)
    axes[1, 1].plot(qq[0][0], qq[1][0] * qq[0][0] + qq[1][1], "r--", lw=2)
    axes[1, 1].set_title("Q–Q plot")
    axes[1, 1].set_xlabel("Theoretical quantiles")
    axes[1, 1].set_ylabel("Sample quantiles")

    # Turn off empty subplot
    axes[1, 2].axis("off")

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def fit_lognormal_glm(
    x_train: pd.Series,
    y_train: pd.Series
) -> Tuple[sm.GLM, pd.Series]:
    """Fit a lognormal GLM using time as covariate.

    The model assumes Y ~ Lognormal and fits a Gaussian GLM on log(Y),
    enabling statistical inference and prediction.

    Args:
        x_train: Training covariate (time).
        y_train: Training response variable (positive, continuous).
        x_test: Test covariate (time).

    Returns:
        A tuple containing:
            - Fitted GLM results object.
    """
    if (y_train <= 0).any():
        raise ValueError("Response variable must be strictly positive.")

    x_train_const = sm.add_constant(x_train)

    log_y_train = np.log(y_train)

    model = sm.GLM(
        log_y_train,
        x_train_const,
        family=sm.families.Gaussian(),
    )

    results = model.fit()

    return results


def summarize_arima_model(
    model_result: ARIMAResults,
    model_name: str,
    y_train: Optional[pd.Series] = None,
    y_test: Optional[pd.Series] = None,
    y_pred_train: Optional[pd.Series] = None,
    y_pred_test: Optional[pd.Series] = None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Create a summary table with ARIMA information and metrics.

    This function gathers AIC, BIC and (optionally) regression metrics
    for train and test sets.

    Args:
        model_result: Fitted ARIMAResults object.
        model_name: Name or identifier of the model, for example
            "ARIMA(1,1,1)".
        y_train: True target values for the training set.
        y_test: True target values for the test set.
        y_pred_train: Predicted values on the training set.
        y_pred_test: Predicted values on the test set.

    Returns:
        A pandas DataFrame with one row containing model name, AIC, BIC
        and available metrics (train_*, test_*).

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If the model does not provide aic or bic
            attributes.
    """
    if not hasattr(model_result, "aic") or not hasattr(
        model_result,
        "bic",
    ):
        raise AttributeError(
            "Model must have 'aic' and 'bic' attributes."
        )

    data: Dict[str, float] = {
        "model": model_name,
        "aic": float(model_result.aic),
        "bic": float(model_result.bic),
    }

    if y_train is not None and y_pred_train is not None:
        train_metrics = compute_regression_metrics(
            y_true=y_train,
            y_pred=y_pred_train,
            prefix="train_",
        )
        data.update(train_metrics)

    if y_test is not None and y_pred_test is not None:
        test_metrics = compute_regression_metrics(
            y_true=y_test,
            y_pred=y_pred_test,
            prefix="test_",
        )
        data.update(test_metrics)

    summary_df = pd.DataFrame([data])

    return summary_df


def compute_regression_metrics(
    y_true: pd.Series,
    y_pred: pd.Series,
    prefix: str = ""
) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Compute common regression metrics for time series.

    The function calculates MAE, RMSE and MAPE. It expects y_true and
    y_pred to be aligned on the same index.

    Args:
        y_true: True target values as a pandas Series.
        y_pred: Predicted target values as a pandas Series.
        prefix: Optional prefix to add to each metric name in the
            returned dictionary (for example "train_" or "test_").

    Returns:
        Dictionary with metrics as keys and their values as floats.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If y_true and y_pred do not have the same length
            or if y_true contains only zeros when computing MAPE.
        TypeError: If y_true or y_pred are not pandas Series.
    """
    if not isinstance(y_true, pd.Series):
        raise TypeError("Parameter 'y_true' must be a pandas Series.")
    if not isinstance(y_pred, pd.Series):
        raise TypeError("Parameter 'y_pred' must be a pandas Series.")

    if len(y_true) != len(y_pred):
        raise ValueError(
            "y_true and y_pred must have the same length."
        )

    # Align indices just in case
    y_true, y_pred = y_true.align(y_pred, join="inner")

    mae = mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred)

    # Older versions of scikit-learn do not support 'squared' argument,
    # so we compute RMSE manually as the square root of MSE.
    mse = mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred)
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(mse))

    if np.any(y_true == 0):
        raise ValueError(
            "MAPE is undefined when y_true contains zeros."
        )

    mape = float(
        np.mean(np.abs((y_true - y_pred) / y_true)) * 100.0
    )

    metrics: Dict[str, float] = {
        f"{prefix}mae": float(mae),
        f"{prefix}rmse": rmse,
        f"{prefix}mape": mape,
    }

    return metrics
```

## GLM Lognormal com tempo e AR(3)


```{python}
resid_ar1_train = residuals_train.shift(1)
resid_ar2_train = residuals_train.shift(2)
resid_ar3_train = residuals_train.shift(3)
resid_ar1_test  = residuals_test.shift(1)
resid_ar2_test  = residuals_test.shift(2)
resid_ar3_test  = residuals_test.shift(3)

X_train_glarma = sm.add_constant(
    pd.DataFrame({"time": X_train,
    "resid_ar1": resid_ar1_train,
    "resid_ar2": resid_ar2_train,
    "resid_ar3": resid_ar3_train}))
X_test_glarma  = sm.add_constant(
    pd.DataFrame({"time": X_test,
    "resid_ar1": resid_ar1_test,
    "resid_ar2": resid_ar2_test,
    "resid_ar3": resid_ar3_test}))

log_y_train = np.log(y_train)

model_glarma = sm.GLM(
    log_y_train, X_train_glarma, family=sm.families.Gaussian(),
    missing="drop").fit()
model_glarma.summary()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame({"AIC": [model_glarma.aic], "BIC": [model_glarma.bic]}, index=["GLM Lognormal (time + resid_ar1,2,3)"])
```

```{python}
    y_true=y_train, y_pred=y_pred_train_glarma)
metrics_test_glarma  = calculate_metrics(
    y_true=y_test,  y_pred=y_pred_test_glarma)
```

## Predições para o conjunto de teste

```{python}

coef_time = model_glarma.params["time"]
coef_ar1 = model_glarma.params["resid_ar1"]
coef_ar2 = model_glarma.params["resid_ar2"]
coef_ar3 = model_glarma.params["resid_ar3"]
```

```{python}
X_pred_glarma["const"] = glarma_cte

    X_pred_glarma.index - start_time).total_seconds()

y_pred_test_glarma = pd.DataFrame()

y_pred_test_glarma

y_test_glarma = y_test[:horizonte]
```

```{python}
X_pred_glarma.loc[X_pred_glarma.index[0], "resid_ar1"] = (
    X_train_glarma.loc[X_train_glarma.index[-1], "resid_ar1"] *
    coef_ar1)
X_pred_glarma.loc[X_pred_glarma.index[0], "resid_ar2"] = (
    X_train_glarma.loc[X_train_glarma.index[-1], "resid_ar2"] *
    coef_ar2)
X_pred_glarma.loc[X_pred_glarma.index[0], "resid_ar3"] = (
    X_train_glarma.loc[X_train_glarma.index[-1], "resid_ar3"] *
    coef_ar3)
y_pred_test_glarma.loc[X_pred_glarma.index[0], "pred"] = np.exp(
    glarma_cte +
    coef_time * X_pred_glarma.loc[
        X_pred_glarma.index[0], "time"] +
    coef_ar1 * X_pred_glarma.loc[
        X_pred_glarma.index[0], "resid_ar1"] +
    coef_ar2 * X_pred_glarma.loc[
        X_pred_glarma.index[0], "resid_ar2"] +
    coef_ar3 * X_pred_glarma.loc[
        X_pred_glarma.index[0], "resid_ar3"]
)

for i in range(1, len(X_pred_glarma)):
    X_pred_glarma.loc[X_pred_glarma.index[i], "resid_ar1"] = (
        X_pred_glarma.loc[
            X_pred_glarma.index[i - 1], "resid_ar1"] *
        coef_ar1)
    X_pred_glarma.loc[X_pred_glarma.index[i], "resid_ar2"] = (
        X_pred_glarma.loc[
            X_pred_glarma.index[i - 1], "resid_ar2"] *
        coef_ar2)
    X_pred_glarma.loc[X_pred_glarma.index[i], "resid_ar3"] = (
        X_pred_glarma.loc[
            X_pred_glarma.index[i - 1], "resid_ar3"] *
        coef_ar3)
    y_pred_test_glarma.loc[X_pred_glarma.index[i], "pred"] = \
        np.exp(
            glarma_cte +
            coef_time * X_pred_glarma.loc[
                X_pred_glarma.index[i], "time"] +
            coef_ar1 * X_pred_glarma.loc[
                X_pred_glarma.index[i], "resid_ar1"] +
            coef_ar2 * X_pred_glarma.loc[
                X_pred_glarma.index[i], "resid_ar2"] +
            coef_ar3 * X_pred_glarma.loc[
                X_pred_glarma.index[i], "resid_ar3"]
        )
```

## Simulação de cenário em Produção: Predição com janela móvel para o Conjunto de Teste

```{python}
# Simulação de cenário de produção: predições rolling 1-step-ahead
# Usando o modelo GLM Lognormal com tempo e AR(3) nos resíduos

# Obter os últimos resíduos do treino para inicializar
last_residuals = residuals_train.iloc[-3:].values  # [resid_{t-3}, resid_{t-2}, resid_{t-1}]

rolling_predictions = []
rolling_actuals = []

X_test_rolling = X_test.iloc[:horizonte]
y_test_rolling = y_test.iloc[:horizonte]

for t in range(len(y_test_rolling)):
    # Preparar X para predição: const, time, resid_ar1, resid_ar2, resid_ar3
    current_time = X_test_rolling.iloc[t]
    X_current = pd.DataFrame({
        'const': [1.0],
        'time': [current_time],
        'resid_ar1': [last_residuals[2]],  # resid_{t-1}
        'resid_ar2': [last_residuals[1]],  # resid_{t-2}
        'resid_ar3': [last_residuals[0]],  # resid_{t-3}
    })
    
    # Predição no log-scale
    log_y_pred = model_glarma.predict(X_current).iloc[0]
    y_pred = np.exp(log_y_pred)
    
    # Valor atual observado
    y_actual = y_test_rolling.iloc[t]
    
    # Computar residual: log(y_actual) - log(y_pred)
    residual = np.log(y_actual) - log_y_pred
    
    # Armazenar predição e atual
    rolling_predictions.append(y_pred)
    rolling_actuals.append(y_actual)
    
    # Atualizar os últimos resíduos para o próximo passo
    last_residuals = np.roll(last_residuals, -1)  # Shift para esquerda
    last_residuals[-1] = residual  # Novo residual na posição mais recente

# Criar séries pandas para o horizonte definido
rolling_pred_series = pd.Series(rolling_predictions, index=y_test_rolling.index, name='Rolling Prediction')
rolling_actual_series = pd.Series(rolling_actuals, index=y_test_rolling.index, name='Actual')

# Plot da predição rolling
plot_forecast_vs_actual(
    y_train=y_train,
    y_test=rolling_actual_series,
    y_pred_test=rolling_pred_series,
    model_name="GLM Lognormal Rolling (Produção)",
)
```

```{python}
# Métricas para a predição rolling
metrics_rolling = calculate_metrics(
    y_true=rolling_actual_series, 
    y_pred=rolling_pred_series
)
metrics_rolling
```
